**Brasília** (/brəˈzɪliə/;[[4]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-5)[[5]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-6) Portuguese: [bɾaˈziljɐ]) is the [federal capital](Federal_capital "Federal capital") of <Brazil> and seat of [government](Forms_of_government "Forms of government") of the [Federal District](Federal_District_(Brazil) "Federal District (Brazil)"). The city is located high in the [Brazilian highlands](Brazilian_highlands "Brazilian highlands") in the country's [Central-West](Central-West_Region%2C_Brazil "Central-West Region, Brazil") region. It was founded by President [Juscelino Kubitschek](Juscelino_Kubitschek "Juscelino Kubitschek") on 21 April 1960, to serve as the new national capital. Brasília is estimated to be Brazil's [third-most populous city](List_of_largest_cities_in_Brazil "List of largest cities in Brazil") after [São Paulo](S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo") and [Rio de Janeiro](Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro").[[2]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-pop-3) Among major [Latin American](Latin_American "Latin American") cities, it has the highest [GDP](Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") per capita.[[6]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-7)

Brasília was a [planned city](Planned_community "Planned community") developed by [Lúcio Costa](L%C3%BAcio_Costa "Lúcio Costa"), [Oscar Niemeyer](Oscar_Niemeyer "Oscar Niemeyer") and [Joaquim Cardozo](Joaquim_Cardozo "Joaquim Cardozo") in 1956 in a scheme to move the capital from [Rio de Janeiro](Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro") to a more central location. The landscape architect was [Roberto Burle Marx](Roberto_Burle_Marx "Roberto Burle Marx").[[7]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-8)[[8]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-9) The city's design divides it into numbered blocks as well as sectors for specified activities, such as the Hotel Sector, the Banking Sector, and the Embassy Sector. Brasília was inscribed as a UNESCO [World Heritage Site](World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") in 1987 due to its [modernist architecture](Modernist_architecture "Modernist architecture") and uniquely artistic [urban planning](Urban_planning "Urban planning").[[9]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-10) It was named "City of Design" by <UNESCO> in October 2017 and has been part of the [Creative Cities Network](Creative_Cities_Network "Creative Cities Network") since then.[[10]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-11)

Brasília is a planned city distinguished by its white, modern architecture, designed by Oscar Niemeyer. All three branches of [Brazil's federal government](Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil") are centered in the city: [executive](President_of_Brazil "President of Brazil"), [legislative](National_Congress_of_Brazil "National Congress of Brazil") and [judiciary](Supreme_Federal_Court "Supreme Federal Court"). Brasília also hosts 124 foreign [embassies](Embassies "Embassies").[[11]](Bras%C3%ADlia#cite_note-12) The city's [international airport](Bras%C3%ADlia_International_Airport "Brasília International Airport") connects it to all other major Brazilian cities and some international destinations, and it is the [third-busiest airport in Brazil](List_of_the_busiest_airports_in_Brazil "List of the busiest airports in Brazil"). It was one of the main host cities of the [2014 FIFA World Cup](2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup") and hosted some of the [football matches during the 2016 Summer Olympics](Football_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Football at the 2016 Summer Olympics"); it also hosted the [2013 FIFA Confederations Cup](2013_FIFA_Confederations_Cup "2013 FIFA Confederations Cup").

Laid out in the shape of an airplane, its "fuselage" is the Monumental Axis, 2 wide avenues flanking a massive park. The city has a unique status in Brazil, as it is an administrative division rather than a legal municipality like other [cities in Brazil](List_of_cities_in_Brazil "List of cities in Brazil"). Brasília is used as a synonym for the Federal District (official name of the federation unity), which is composed of [33 administrative regions](List_of_administrative_regions_of_the_Federal_District_(Brazil) "List of administrative regions of the Federal District (Brazil)"), one of which is the area of the originally planned city, called *Plano Piloto*. In the "cockpit" is Praça dos Três Poderes, named for the 3 branches of government surrounding it. This unique structure exists because Brasília was specifically designed as the federal capital with all three branches of Brazil's federal government (executive, legislative, and judiciary) centered in the city. The Federal District encompasses Brasília and its 32 other administrative regions.
